questions.stem: These paired breast sections show tumor cells infiltrating in a single-file pattern (left, H&E) and absence of the membranous brown immunostain seen normally (right). The loss of the marker highlighted here most directly impairs which cellular function?

explanation.summary: The single-file infiltration and loss of membranous staining reflect loss of E-cadherin, a homophilic adhesion molecule; its loss disrupts cell-to-cell adhesion, a hallmark of invasive lobular carcinoma. The other functions are unrelated to E-cadherin.
explanation.whyCorrect: The single-file infiltration and loss of membranous staining reflect loss of E-cadherin, a homophilic adhesion molecule; its loss disrupts cell-to-cell adhesion, a hallmark of invasive lobular carcinoma. The other functions are unrelated to E-cadherin.

questions.stem: This uterine sarcoma shows a rounded nest of neoplastic cells filling and expanding a vascular space. A tumor demonstrating this pattern of spread would be expected to metastasize primarily by which route?

explanation.summary: Sarcomas of mesenchymal origin invade vessels and characteristically metastasize hematogenously, as shown by tumor filling the vascular lumen. Lymphatic spread is typical of carcinomas, transcoelomic seeding occurs across body cavities, and perineural/direct extension are different routes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sarcomas of mesenchymal origin invade vessels and characteristically metastasize hematogenously, as shown by tumor filling the vascular lumen. Lymphatic spread is typical of carcinomas, transcoelomic seeding occurs across body cavities, and perineural/direct extension are different routes.

questions.stem: This gross specimen shows the omentum diffusely studded and thickened by nodular tumor deposits. By which mechanism of spread did the ovarian carcinoma most likely reach this site?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hematogenous spread through the portal vein

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct invasion through the uterine wall

explanation.summary: Ovarian carcinoma classically seeds the peritoneal cavity, coating the omentum with tumor (omental caking) via transcoelomic spread. The other routes do not explain diffuse serosal/omental studding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ovarian carcinoma classically seeds the peritoneal cavity, coating the omentum with tumor (omental caking) via transcoelomic spread. The other routes do not explain diffuse serosal/omental studding.

questions.stem: This mnemonic figure maps chemotherapy agents to their signature organ toxicities. The agent depicted as causing hemorrhagic cystitis produces a bladder-toxic metabolite; co-administration of which agent prevents this toxicity?

explanation.summary: Cyclophosphamide generates acrolein, which injures the bladder urothelium and causes hemorrhagic cystitis. Mesna binds and detoxifies acrolein in the urine. Leucovorin rescues methotrexate toxicity, amifostine protects against cisplatin nephro/ototoxicity, and dexrazoxane guards against anthracycline cardiotoxicity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyclophosphamide generates acrolein, which injures the bladder urothelium and causes hemorrhagic cystitis. Mesna binds and detoxifies acrolein in the urine. Leucovorin rescues methotrexate toxicity, amifostine protects against cisplatin nephro/ototoxicity, and dexrazoxane guards against anthracycline cardiotoxicity.

questions.stem: This two-panel figure contrasts tumor immunity with and without antibodies directed against CTLA-4 and PD-1/PD-L1, showing restored cytotoxic T cell killing when the antibodies are used. What general class of cancer therapy does this illustrate?

explanation.summary: Blocking inhibitory checkpoint pathways (CTLA-4 and PD-1/PD-L1) with antibodies removes the brakes on T cells, restoring their ability to activate and kill tumor cells. This checkpoint blockade approach is approved for advanced solid tumors and some lymphomas.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blocking inhibitory checkpoint pathways (CTLA-4 and PD-1/PD-L1) with antibodies removes the brakes on T cells, restoring their ability to activate and kill tumor cells. This checkpoint blockade approach is approved for advanced solid tumors and some lymphomas.

questions.stem: The tumor cell on the left has lost a specific surface molecule, and as a result the T cell on the right is unable to recognize it. The absence of this molecule most directly impairs which immune function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recognition and killing by cytotoxic CD8+ T cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Helper CD4+ T cell cytokine release

choices.label: E
choices.text: Activation of the classical complement pathway

explanation.summary: The tumor is MHC class I-deficient. Because cytotoxic T cells identify targets via antigen presented on MHC class I, loss of this molecule allows the tumor to escape CD8+ T cell-mediated killing.
explanation.whyCorrect: The tumor is MHC class I-deficient. Because cytotoxic T cells identify targets via antigen presented on MHC class I, loss of this molecule allows the tumor to escape CD8+ T cell-mediated killing.
